name: Recover deficiencies and approve write-offs
summary: When a defaulted lease cannot be cured, or the repossessed equipment sells for less than the balance, a recovery officer turns the remaining amount into a deficiency file. The officer calculates what is still owed, sends a deficiency statement and a demand to the customer and the personal guarantors, negotiates settlements, traces owners and their assets, and recommends a write-off that the recovery manager reviews and the director or the chief credit and risk officer approves. After the charge-off is posted the file goes to a collection agency, to legal for a guarantor lawsuit, or is closed, and charged-off securitised contracts are reported to treasury. Waiting for sale settlements, unanswered demands, skip tracing and monthly approval batches make the process slow, and most files recover little.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 55,000 active small- and mid-ticket contracts and a five-person recoveries and insolvency team.
baseline.notes: Commercial leases and loans only; the consumer seize-or-sue rules do not apply. Deficiency files come from late-stage write-off and insolvency referrals and from sales of repossessed equipment.

trigger: Late-stage collections sends an approved write-off request, the sale proceeds of repossessed equipment are applied leaving a balance, or legal reports a recovery on a charged-off account.
end_state: The deficiency is charged off with approval and placed with an agency, referred to legal or closed; or the balance is recovered in full; or a recovery is applied to an account already charged off.

volume.seasonality: Rose through 2020 as COVID payment deferrals ended and delinquency climbed; flat by month otherwise, with write-off approvals bunched before month-end.

evidence.note: Organisation file range of 50 to 110. Late-stage collections sends about 5% of 650 accounts as write-off requests and 4% as insolvency referrals (efc-collect-late-stage), and most of about 45 repossessions a month leave a deficiency, which puts the mode near 75.

Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). About 2.3 of the 4 recovery officers' time; the rest goes to repossessions and insolvency files. Senior collector wage band from Job Bank.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Settlement and write-off reviews plus agency oversight; the manager also runs repossessions and insolvency files with legal.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Monthly write-off approvals of about an hour per batch plus escalations.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Signs the few write-offs above the director's limit.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Document imaging and contract file store
Commercial and consumer credit bureau portals (Equifax, PayNet)
Federal and provincial corporate registry searches (web and search-provider portals)
Provincial personal property registry and Quebec RDPRM search and registration portals
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)

steps.name: Move the account to the recovery queue
steps.description: When late-stage collections sends an approved write-off request, when the sale proceeds of repossessed equipment are posted, or when legal reports a recovery, the collections system moves the contract into the recovery queue and assigns it to a recovery officer by region and balance, with earlier notes attached.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Queue routing by a collections system is the common set-up; nightly batch timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Review the incoming file
steps.description: The recovery officer reads the late-stage memo or the remarketing settlement note, the contract and schedules, the personal guarantees, the default notice history and any earlier settlement talks, and decides what the file needs: a deficiency calculation, missing sale figures, or just the posting of a recovery from legal or an agency.

error.defect_description: Guarantor or second contract overlooked.

next.condition: post-sale file missing the final sale statement or cost invoices
file ready for the deficiency calculation
update from legal or an agency on a charged-off account

evidence.note: Branch shares are author estimates from the trigger mix (about 55% write-off requests, 36% post-sale files, 9% legal recoveries).

steps.name: Collect the final sale statement and cost invoices
steps.description: For equipment that was repossessed and sold, the officer asks remarketing for the auction or buyer settlement statement and asks accounts payable for the bailiff, transport, storage, repair and legal invoices, because the deficiency cannot be stated until every cost is known. Late auction settlements and invoices are chased by email.

error.defect_description: A late storage or legal invoice is missed and the deficiency is understated.

evidence.note: Waits for auction settlements and supplier invoices are author estimates; auction settlement usually follows a sale within about two weeks.

steps.name: Calculate the deficiency balance
steps.description: In a spreadsheet the officer works out the balance owed under the default clause: arrears, accelerated future rents discounted at the contract rate, the purchase option or residual, late charges and taxes, plus repossession, storage, repair, selling and legal costs, less net sale proceeds and any security deposit. Figures are re-keyed from the lease system, the settlement statement and invoices.

error.defect_description: Wrong discount rate, a missed credit or a cost charged twice.

evidence.note: The content of the calculation is described in the sources; times and the error rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Check insolvency records, credit bureau and corporate status
steps.description: Before demanding payment the officer searches the federal insolvency records for the business and each guarantor, refreshes the commercial and personal bureau reports and checks whether the corporation is still active. A bankruptcy, proposal or notice of intention stops all collection contact and sends the file down the claim route.

error.defect_description: A recent filing is missed and a stayed debtor is contacted.

control.basis: Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act s.69 and s.69.3: stay of proceedings once a notice of intention, proposal or bankruptcy is filed

next.condition: insolvency filing found or already flagged by late-stage collections

evidence.note: Late-stage collections refers about 4% of its accounts to recoveries because of insolvency (efc-collect-late-stage); the 25% share here is the author's estimate of those plus new filings.

steps.name: Send the deficiency statement and demand
steps.description: The officer fills the deficiency letter template with the disposition details (date, method, price), the calculation and the amount due, and a deadline of about 15 days, and sends a demand under each personal guarantee. Letters go by registered mail or courier and email, and proof of delivery is filed because the demand starts the guarantor's obligation and the limitation clock.

error.defect_description: A guarantor's current address is wrong and the demand is not delivered.

control.basis: Provincial PPSA rules on disposition and accounting to the debtor (BC PPSA ss.59-60; a debtor can raise non-compliance as a defence to a deficiency claim, s.69(7)), the guarantee's demand clause and the two-year Ontario Limitations Act period

evidence.note: The 15-day deadline is an author estimate.

steps.name: Customer and guarantors respond to the demand
steps.description: The demand period runs. Some owners call to dispute the sale price or the costs, some offer a settlement or instalments, and most do not reply, often because the business has closed and the owners have few assets left.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: customer disputes the sale or the balance
customer or guarantor wants to negotiate

evidence.note: Response shares are author estimates; sources describe most deficiency debtors as hard to reach after the business fails.

steps.name: Investigate a dispute about the sale or the balance
steps.description: The officer pulls the condition report, the auction results, the notice of intended disposition and its proof of delivery and the cost invoices, asks remarketing whether the sale was in line with the market, corrects any error in the calculation and replies in writing.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: calculation corrected and a revised statement sent
dispute rejected and the customer stops engaging

evidence.note: Rework shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Negotiate a settlement or payment plan
steps.description: The officer talks with the owner or guarantor about a lump-sum settlement at a discount or instalments over several months, checks what they own from bureau data and property searches, and compares the offer with what an agency or a lawsuit would net after fees and costs.

error.defect_description: A settlement is offered below what the guarantor could pay.

next.condition: discounted settlement or a plan beyond the officer's limit
full-balance plan within the officer's authority

evidence.note: Branch shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve the settlement offer
steps.description: The recovery and insolvency manager reviews the offer against the balance, the guarantor's means, the expected agency or legal recovery and the delegated settlement limits, and approves it, asks for a better offer, or notes that the forgiven amount needs the director when the write-off is approved.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Collections policy: delegated authority to compromise a debt

evidence.note: Delegated settlement approval is common practice; times and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm the settlement and set up payments
steps.description: The officer sends a written settlement agreement that keeps the full claim alive if payments stop, records the amounts and dates in the collections system and sets up a pre-authorised debit or asks for a certified cheque or wire for a lump sum.

error.defect_description: Payment schedule keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the settlement payments
steps.description: The file waits for the lump sum or the instalments. Lump sums usually arrive within weeks; instalment plans run for months and the collections system flags any missed payment for follow-up.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: discounted settlement paid; the shortfall is written off

evidence.note: Plan lengths and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Trace the customer and guarantors and search for assets
steps.description: For silent or broken files the officer traces the owners and guarantors through bureau addresses, corporate records and online searches, checks for real property, vehicles and other registrations, and decides the route: an agency placement, a lawsuit on the guarantee where there is equity worth pursuing, or no action where nothing is recoverable.

error.defect_description: Assets missed, so a viable guarantor claim goes to an agency or is closed.

evidence.note: Charter writes off only after it has determined the client lacks assets; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the write-off recommendation
steps.description: The officer writes the write-off memo: balance and deficiency calculation, collection and settlement history, asset search results, guarantor position, any insolvency claim, the recommended route and expected recovery, and the tax portion that can be recovered through the GST/HST bad debt deduction.

error.defect_description: Memo incomplete or the amount does not match the lease system.

evidence.note: Memo content follows the write-off test in the sources; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review the write-off recommendation
steps.description: The recovery and insolvency manager checks that the collection steps were exhausted, the demand letters and notices are on file, the amount ties to the lease system and the route makes sense, then signs and adds the file to the director's write-off list or sends it back.

error.defect_description: An incomplete file is passed.

control.basis: Credit and collections policy: file completeness review before write-off

next.condition: returned for more collection or search work

evidence.note: Two-level review of write-offs is common practice; the return rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Approve the write-off
steps.description: At the monthly write-off review the director of collections and recoveries goes through the list with the manager and approves write-offs within the director's delegated limit, sends larger ones to the chief credit and risk officer and occasionally asks for another attempt.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Board-approved delegated write-off authority; IFRS 9 paragraph 5.4.4 (write off when there is no reasonable expectation of recovery)

evidence.note: The organisation file says write-offs need the director or the chief credit and risk officer; the monthly batch and the limit split are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve a write-off above the director's limit
steps.description: The chief credit and risk officer reviews large write-offs, usually mid-ticket contracts or files with guarantor litigation, asks about remaining recovery options and signs the approval or sends the file back.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Escalation share and timing are author estimates.

steps.name: Post the charge-off in the lease system
steps.description: With the signed approval the officer enters the charge-off transaction in the lease system, stops billing and late charges, sets the contract status to charged off and records the tax portion so tax can claim the GST/HST bad debt deduction. The approval memo is attached in imaging for audit.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount or tax split posted.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: charge-offs posted only against a documented approval; Excise Tax Act s.231 requires the debt to be written off in the books before the tax is deducted

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Post the charge-off journal and update portfolio data
steps.description: The nightly interface posts the charge-off against the loss allowance in the general ledger and loads the contract's new status, charge-off amount and recovery route into the data warehouse used by risk, treasury and accounting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: contract sits in a securitised pool
not securitised; place with an agency
not securitised; nothing recoverable or the trustee holds the claim

evidence.note: About 62% of receivables sit in conduit pools (organisation file says about 65%).

steps.name: Notify treasury of the charged-off securitised contract
steps.description: The officer adds the contract to the weekly list of charged-off and recovered securitised contracts sent to the securitisation analyst, with pool code, balance at default, sale proceeds and expected recoveries, so the servicer report shows the default and any repurchase or substitution.

error.defect_description: Contract left off the list and the servicer report understates defaults.

control.basis: Conduit servicing agreement: servicer reports defaulted and charged-off receivables and recoveries each period

next.condition: nothing recoverable or the trustee holds the claim

evidence.note: Servicer reports show defaults and recoveries each period; the weekly list is an author estimate.

steps.name: Place the deficiency with a collection agency
steps.description: The officer uploads the placement to the panel agency's portal or by secure email: statement of account, contract, guarantees, demand letters, last known contacts and asset search, and records the placement, the contingency fee rate and the review date in the collections system.

error.defect_description: Placement missing a guarantor or document.

evidence.note: Placement after write-off and weekly placement batches are author estimates.

steps.name: Refer the file to legal for a guarantor action
steps.description: Where a guarantor owns real property or the balance is large, the officer prepares a legal referral: chronology, contract and guarantee, demand and proof of delivery, deficiency calculation, sale records and asset search, so in-house counsel can sue or instruct outside lawyers before the limitation period runs.

error.defect_description: Referral missing proof of the demand or the disposition notice.

control.basis: Ontario Limitations Act, 2002: two-year basic limitation period for the claim against the customer and guarantors

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the insolvency claim package for legal
steps.description: For a customer or guarantor in bankruptcy or a proposal, the officer prepares the statement of account and supporting documents for the proof of claim (the lessor's or secured creditor's claim, payments in the last three months) and sends it to legal, who files it with the trustee.

error.defect_description: Claim amount or class wrong.

control.basis: Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act: Form 31 proof of claim with a statement of account, filed with the trustee to share in any dividend

next.condition: claim package sent; write-off recommended with the expected dividend

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Apply a legal or agency recovery to a charged-off account
steps.description: When legal reports a judgment payment or settlement, or an agency remits collections net of its fee, the officer matches the statement to the charged-off contract, posts the recovery in the lease system and records the tax on the recovered amount so it is added back on the next GST/HST return.

error.defect_description: Recovery posted to the wrong contract or gross instead of net of fees.

control.basis: Excise Tax Act s.231(3): tax on a recovered bad debt is added back to net tax

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve the recovery posting and the agency or lawyer's fee
steps.description: The recovery and insolvency manager checks the posting against the remittance statement, approves the contingency fee or legal invoice for payment and decides whether the file stays open with the agency or lawyer or can be closed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control: the person posting a recovery does not approve the related fee payment

next.condition: partial recovery; file stays with the agency or lawyer
balance or agreed settlement fully recovered

evidence.note: Common internal-control practice; shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Close the file and confirm to the customer
steps.description: When the balance or an agreed settlement is paid, the officer closes the file in the collections system, ends any agency placement, sends the customer and guarantors a confirmation that the debt is settled and asks lease administration to discharge any remaining registration.

error.defect_description: Agency not told to stop and keeps contacting the customer.

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Missing sale statement or cost invoices
exceptions.description: The auction settlement or the bailiff, storage or legal invoices are not in, so the officer chases them before the deficiency can be stated.

exceptions.name: Insolvency filing
exceptions.description: The customer or a guarantor is in bankruptcy, a proposal or a notice of intention; collection stops and a claim package goes to legal before the write-off.

exceptions.name: Disputed deficiency
exceptions.description: The customer challenges the sale price or the costs; the officer investigates and may reissue the statement.

exceptions.name: Broken settlement
exceptions.description: Settlement or plan payments stop and the file returns to tracing and the write-off route.

exceptions.name: Write-off returned
exceptions.description: The manager, director or chief credit and risk officer sends the file back for more collection or asset search work.

exceptions.name: Large write-off
exceptions.description: The write-off exceeds the director's limit and needs the chief credit and risk officer.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the file entering the recovery queue to charge-off and placement, full recovery or recovery posting

evidence.note: Author estimate: demand periods of two to four weeks, tracing, monthly write-off approval and weeks of waiting for sale settlements. Charter wrote off only after enforcement steps had been taken.

benchmarks.population: US equipment finance companies, 104 ELFA respondents

evidence.note: Or charged off earlier by the servicer.

benchmarks.unit: years after the return period of the write-off

pain_points.description: The deficiency letter waits for the auction settlement and the bailiff, storage and legal invoices, which arrive over several weeks.

evidence.note: Author estimate from the sequence of repossession, sale and supplier billing.

pain_points.description: Balances are recalculated by hand in spreadsheets from lease system figures, and calculation errors surface only when a customer disputes the amount.

evidence.note: The source stresses documenting the deficiency calculation to avoid disputes.

pain_points.description: Most demands go unanswered; demand periods and skip tracing add weeks to files that end in write-off anyway.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Write-offs are approved in a monthly batch, so files queue for up to a month before posting.

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Agency and legal recoveries arrive as remittance statements that are re-keyed contract by contract.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: Personal Property Security Act [RSBC 1996] chapter 359
sources.supports: s.59(6): notice at least 20 days before disposing of seized collateral; s.60(3): written accounting of the disposition within 30 days after a written demand; s.60(5): the debtor is liable to pay any deficiency; s.69(7): non-compliance with ss.59 and 60 can be raised as a defence to a deficiency claim; s.67: seize-or-sue rule applies to consumer goods only.

sources.title: Excise Tax Act, section 231 (bad debts)
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: A supplier that writes off a bad debt on a taxable supply to an arm's-length recipient may deduct the tax portion from net tax (s.231(1)); tax on a later recovery must be added back (s.231(3)); the deduction must be claimed within four years (s.231(4)).

sources.title: Removal of irrecoverable receivables from the asset
sources.publisher: Banco Central de la Republica Argentina
sources.supports: Restates IFRS 9 paragraph 5.4.4: a write-off applies when the entity has no reasonable expectation of recovering contractual cash flows, is a derecognition event, and written-off assets still under enforcement are disclosed under IFRS 7 35L.

sources.title: Charter Equipment Lease 1998-1 LLC prospectus (Form 424B1)
sources.supports: A New York and Toronto equipment lessor writes a transaction off only after reasonable steps to enforce its remedies show the client lacks assets, and pursues any deficiency after repossession and sale to the extent practicable; defaulted leases are those more than 120 days delinquent or charged off; servicer reports show recoveries on defaulted leases each period.

sources.title: Preserving and collecting a deficiency balance after repo and sale
sources.supports: Post-sale deficiency notice stating the amount and how it was calculated; collection runs from negotiation (lump sum or plan) to litigation to post-judgment remedies; commercially reasonable sale needed to keep the deficiency claim (US UCC context).

sources.title: The Collector Chronicles: beyond the default, how lenders master repossession and recovery
sources.supports: After sale, proceeds are applied and the remaining amount becomes a deficiency handled by repayment plans, placement with agencies or counsel for larger balances, or charge-off when pursuit is not economical; clear documentation of the deficiency calculation prevents disputes.

sources.title: Limitation periods on guarantees (Aird & Berlis LLP)
sources.supports: Ontario Limitations Act, 2002: two-year basic limitation period from discovery; in Chorny the period on a guarantee ran from the principal debtor's default, so lenders must act on guarantees within two years unless the documents extend the period.

sources.title: Form 31, Proof of Claim
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Bankruptcy Canada
sources.supports: A creditor's proof of claim attaches a statement of account specifying the vouchers or evidence, states whether the claim is unsecured, secured or a lessor's claim, and lists payments received in the three months before the bankruptcy.

sources.title: Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, section 69 (stay of proceedings on a notice of intention)
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Once a notice of intention is filed no creditor has any remedy against the insolvent person or may commence or continue proceedings to recover a claim provable in bankruptcy.

sources.title: New data reveals market insights (2021 Survey of Equipment Finance Activity)
sources.supports: US equipment finance 2020: receivables over 30 days past due 2.3%; net full-year losses 0.48% of average receivables; 104 respondents.

sources.title: Wages: Collector in Ontario (NOC 14202)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages for collectors: low $17.95, median $25.38, high $36.69; Toronto median $27.00 (2023-2024).

assumptions: Volume mode of 75 sits inside the organisation file's range of 50 to 110; late-stage collections' own estimate of about 58 write-off and insolvency referrals a month plus post-sale deficiencies would put it nearer 90.

Late-stage collections sends insolvency referrals with the write_off_request object (as its workflow notes); this file treats them as deficiency files that get a claim package for legal before the write-off.

Insolvency claim packages go to legal at step s23, but the case continues to a write-off; the legal_referral output is tied only to the guarantor-action outcome because the format links outputs to END outcomes.
Write-off approval is modelled as a monthly review, with the director approving most files and the chief credit and risk officer about one in eight; limits are not published and are author estimates.
Post-charge-off agency work and lawsuits are outside this case; recoveries come back as new cases through the legal_recovery trigger (step s24).
Recovery officers' time is shared with repossessions; about 2.3 of 4 officers' time is assigned here.
Legal rules named in controls are the author's reading of the cited statutes and commentary, not legal advice; BC's PPSA text is used where Ontario's statute site could not be opened.
External steps have no touch time; customer replies and payments are in wait_before_min.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
